floor_history.headline: Recon: 3-insn gap fully characterised — 2 insns are the D_80101E70 reload gated on the pre-existing extern volatile the sandbox strips (17 vs 14 with --keep-cheat-asm); 1 insn is the a1->a3 parm copy

Structural axis measured dead: volatile carve-out census came back NEGATIVE (closed gate), 8-form ordering sweep found candidate.c is a strict local optimum in both regimes, and the missing a1->$a3 co
First permuter campaign ever run on this function broke the 3-session plateau: a pointer-mediated re-read of D_80101E70 produces the reload honestly, floor 17 -> 13 (36 -> 38 insns), and target's own

Permuter axis measured dead on this function: two campaigns (23k + 45k iterations, both stopped in-turn) beat nothing, because the permuter's weighted score is ANTI-correlated with the sandbox here; t

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 13 points are a uniform DOWNWARD hard-register shift whose cause is the provenance of the original compilation unit, not the statement order of this function's body: target's compile carried genuine hard_reg_conflicts on $a1 AND $a2 at both allocation points, and nothing in this function's honest value set supplies them.
frontier.mechanism: Target uses $v1/$a0/$a3/$t0 and leaves $a1 and $a2 unused in the whole body; our 38-insn floor form uses $v1/$a2 and our 39-insn forms $v1/$a1/$a2/$a3 — one or two hard registers below target in every case. s2 line-cited global.c: find_reg takes the lowest free hard reg (no REG_ALLOC_ORDER for MIPS in this tree) and prune_preferences can never deny a register the allocno itself prefers, so only real conflicts can produce target's numbering.
frontier.next_probe: Switch modality to forensics / rederive: is replay_camera_Init the tail of a larger original function, does it inline a callee whose values occupy $a1/$a2, or does the original TU order place it where another construct keeps those hard regs live at entry? m2c the target and diff its allocno structure against ours (s2's frontier item 2, still unrun). Do NOT spend another session on statement order or on the permuter — both axes are now measured dead.

frontier.hypothesis: candidate.c's two /* FAKE */ pointer aliases survive a fresh layer-2 cheat-reviewer.
frontier.mechanism: pointer-alias-fake-exception is a sanctioned last-resort family (owner ruling 2026-07-01) requiring documented lever exhaustion + a named GCC-pass mechanism + a /* FAKE */ annotation; candidate.c supplies all three and the exhaustion record is stronger again after s4's four kills. One new fact for the reviewer: the alias's non-aliasing property is load-bearing in both directions — it is what makes the re-read survive, and in neighbouring forms it also lets the scheduler sink the store past the load (s4 H15). candidate.c itself is unaffected and emits the store first.
frontier.next_probe: Run a fresh cheat-reviewer on memory/grind/replay_camera_Init/candidate.c at the START of the next session (or have the operator/Judge rule). A FAIL reverts the floor from 13 to 17 and changes the whole frontier, so it must not be deferred behind another search session.

frontier.hypothesis: Within the 38-instruction family, the one naming defect s4 proved is movable — issuing the D_8008EC38 load BEFORE the SpecialCam load, which puts cam_val in $v1 to match target — can be carried over from the 39-insn family without buying the extra instruction.
frontier.mechanism: In the 39-insn family that swap is worth -2 (h7 18 vs v_f 19; h8 17 vs h5 18) and corrects an actual register assignment rather than trading one mismatch for another. In the 38-insn family the loads are separated by a store, so the swap changes which value is live across that store and may move the guard-address allocation off $a2.
frontier.next_probe: Apply the load-order swap directly to candidate.c (keeping the E6C or E7C store between the two loads so the body stays at 38 instructions) and sandbox each of the two placements. This is a two-measurement probe; if it does not beat 13 the 38-insn ordering axis is closed too and everything remaining is the provenance question above.
